feedback.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-24x+10y=7$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
feedback.worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-24x+10y & =7 \\ 6({x}^{2}-4x)-({y}^{2}-10y) & =7 \\ 6[(x-2)^{2}-4]-[(y-5)^{2}-25] & =7 \\ 6(x-2)^{2}-24-(y-5)^{2}+25 & =7 \\ 6(x-2)^{2}-(y-5)^{2} & =7+24-25 \\ 6(x-2)^{2}-(y-5)^{2} & =6 \\ \frac{(x-2)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(y-5)^{2}}{6}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,2,5\,).$
